old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a modern glass building against a backdrop of a clear blue sky with scattered white clouds. The building's facade is composed of large, reflective glass panels framed by dark metal beams, creating a grid-like pattern. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the architectural details of the building. As the video progresses, the clouds move across the sky, their shapes and positions changing subtly over time. The reflections on the glass panels shift accordingly, mirroring the movement of the clouds and the changing light conditions. The overall scene conveys a sense of tranquility and the interplay between man-made structures and natural elements.

caption: The video captures a low-angle, fixed view of the corner of a modern glass-clad building, where a vertical stone column rises toward a dark recessed notch and a grid of dark mullions frames a mirrored facade. The structure and mullion lines remain steady, so the visible motion comes from the reflected sky. A bright cumulus cloud mass drifts slowly leftward across the right-hand facade, rising slightly as it travels, while a smaller wispy reflection enters at the upper-right edge and slides the same way. The cloud reflections in the angled corner panels move in step, with shapes sliding into and out of the narrower left-side panes. The deep blue sky tone and the dark notch stay constant as the reflected clouds continue their steady passage.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
